utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And that break would have run from 15:10 to 15:40; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If it was asked at 15:10; yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It was asked at 15.10, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Isn't that the time the interview concluded with Dr. Seda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible. I don't know. I can't remember the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the OTP interview began at 15:30; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So Mr. Mucic was not given a 30 minute break, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic was given a break. He went away. I think he went to his cell or to the toilet and came back himself after 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic was allowed to move around by himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was accompanied by guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Tell us what happened during that 20 minute period between Dr. Seda's interview terminating and the OTP interview beginning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think after the interview of Dr. Seda we moved to another room. It was a very small room. We set up the video equipment and the audio equipment and we had problems finding the correct angle for the video camera that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Did anyone from the OTP speak with Mr. Mucic during that period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Before March 18th had you briefed the Austrian police about the Celebici case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Me personally, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Had the OTP briefed the Austrian police, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there was an exchange of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: What was said to the best of your recollection to the Austrian police about the Celebici case by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we gave them a brief summary of what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: When you arrived in Vienna, I assume then as well there was conversation with the Austrian police about Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had a few contacts with the Austrian police about the arrest. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: What else was discussed with the Austrian police after you arrived on 18th? You arrived on the 17th actually, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I arrived on Sunday, 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: What was discussed between 17th and 18th with the Austrian police about this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing about the case. Nothing about the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But you told them why you were there, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: What did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think -- I believe that they knew that we were coming and what we were coming for.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In fact, you were in Vienna to arrange for the extradition of Mr. Mucic back to The Hague, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: What was the purpose of your trip to Vienna then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To interview Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You were aware of the Rule 40 request by the Prosecutor of this Tribunal for provisional arrest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan, do you mind if we have a break? We will resume at 4.30. (4.00 pm) (Short break) (4.30pm) (Witness re-enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly tell him he is on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm reminding you that you are still testifying under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Professor O'Sullivan, you can carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. Sir, I only have a few more questions for you. Before the break we were talking about the reason why you were in Vienna in March of 1996. I suggest to you that you were there to arrange for the extradition of Mr. Mucic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what you said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Then I ask why you were there, therefore, in Vienna, if it was not to arrange for the extradition of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there to interview Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But obviously you were there to interview him with a view to bringing him back to The Hague, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, extradition is something that happens according to the Austrian law. It has nothing to do with the members of -- it's not the duty of the members of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But that brings us back to the briefings and the conversations you had with the Austrian authorities, doesn't it? You were working with them to arrange the extradition of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am an investigator, not a legal adviser. I think that is something for the Legal Department of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: During your talks with the Austrian authorities you did mention the extradition of Mr. Mucic back to The Hague, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only time I heard about extradition was when Dr. Seda informed us that Mr. Mucic asked for a lawyer for his extradition procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The day before Mr. Mucic's interview with you on 19th March was he given any forms by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In that 20 minutes between the meeting with Dr. Seda and your interview with Mr. Mucic on March 19th you say no one from the OTP spoke with Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Abribat spoke to him before the start of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But between that period between the end of Mr. Seda's meeting and the beginning of your meeting, did anyone from the OTP speak with Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think so. Mr. Mucic was not there. He was in his cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So Mr. Abribat did not speak to him either then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Mr. Mucic returned from his cell and entered the room, then Mr. Abribat spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Prior to returning to the room for the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: On June 2nd before this Tribunal in regards to that 20 minute period between Mr. Mucic's meetings with Dr. Seda and the OTP Mr. Abribat sat where you are sitting and said, and I quote: "This is the equipment we're going to use in order to record this hearing. I'm also going to show you the video recorder, saying this is the other piece of equipment that I'm going to use and we'll respect the forms that I gave you yesterday". So if Mr. Abribat said that here under oath on June 2nd, does that mean that he's not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. I think he can ask him if this is a correct statement, but I don't think that he's entitled or should be asked to vouch for anyone's credibility. I think defence counsel asked about at the time what forms meant and it's clear it wasn't paper forms.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If Mr. Abribat said that, is it a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is possible. I'm pretty sure that Mr. Mucic was not given any forms. That I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So in that regard Mr. Abribat is not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Abribat was talking about the form meaning the way in which the interview will be conducted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It is "forms" with an S.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. This witness has not here when Mr. Abribat testified. He has already given his answer. I don't think I can give evidence whether it was "forms" with an S or what Mr. Abribat meant. I believe defence counsel asked Mr. Abribat himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Don't you think it is not fair to ask this witness what Mr. Abribat said? It's not even right to do that. He is not answerable to what Mr. Abribat said.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: From the end of the meeting with Dr. Seda up to the beginning of your meeting with Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Were you with Mr. Abribat the whole time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You have no question to answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Briefly in re-examination, Mr. d'Hooge, do you have anything you want to add to your last answer to clarify or give a more complete answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: That's not a proper question to ask in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually it is not re-examination, is it? That is not in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that this witness and all witnesses should be allowed to give a complete answer, and if counsel doesn't let them finish what they need to give to provide a fair answer, I think I'm entitled to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: No, Ms McHenry, you are not being fair to the procedure. All that happened was Professor Sullivan finished his questions and the witness wasn't satisfied with his answer, but he wasn't asking him any further questions. So there is no point making any answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: All right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: So you can in re-examination know how to put it so that you can get answers if the questions were not properly answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, do you know whether or not during this break whether or not Mr. Abribat had the opportunity to speak with Mr. Mucic privately?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has already answered that question and in any case he says he was not all the time with Mr. Abribat. How can he say anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: For instance, if he knew something about Mr. Mucic and who was in charge of his custody he might be able to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Your question is whether Mr. Abribat met them during those 20 minutes. That was not the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's fine, your Honour. Sir, going back to some questions asked to you, I believe, by Mr. Landzo's defence counsel on interpretation issues, does the recording of the interview of Mr. Esad Landzo contain both the Serbo-Croatian words spoken to and by Mr. Landzo as well as the English words spoken by during the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not interpreters can interpret every single word literally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm pretty sure that they can't.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. When you've talked about interpreters, do you know whether or not interpreters that you've worked with, either with Mr. Landzo's interview or any other interpreters, do you know whether or not they work for the Office of the Prosecutor or the Registry of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe they work for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: With respect to Mr. Landzo's interview, did the interpreter inform you that she could and that she did fairly interpret what you said and what Mr. Landzo said?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to anything that the interpreter might have told him. That's a totally unreliable thing. If the interpreter is going to give testimony here, then I want her here so that I can cross-examine that testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: These are conversations between him and the interpreter. It has nothing to do with this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, can I ask if you're aware of whether or not the translation section of the Tribunal compared the English and Serbo-Croatian version of the transcript and the video to ensure that the translation and transcription were fair and accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, now in response to questions asked by Mr. Moran on behalf of Mr. Delic, I believe you have testified that you had a copy of the indictment when you were in Vienna. Can you indicate when you received this indictment, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure I said we had a copy of the indictment. I think Dr. Manfred, the attorney, asked for a copy of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. When you were in Vienna do you know if you had a copy of an indictment that had been signed by the Prosecutor and confirmed by a judge of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think we had one.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, going to 18th March 1996 in Vienna, when you were at the Vienna police station did you or anyone else from the Tribunal have free access to any of the seized material, or were there always Austrian police officers present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were always Austrian police officers present.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, you stated that after you had selected certain items that you wished photocopied subsequently in the next day or two -- I don't remember exactly what you said -- you received photocopies of the material you had requested. At that time that you received the material, did you receive anything other than the photocopies you had requested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed back in The Hague that instead of receiving only copies, we also received four documents that according to me were original documents.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. I would ask that the witness be shown what has been marked for identification purposes as Prosecution Exhibit 147?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was this shown to the witness during the course of cross-examination? If it wasn't, it's not a proper question in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the issue was raised in cross-examination. I believe that the issue was raised in cross-examination, and therefore we're entitled to go through it. So that's what I believe. If your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What was the question asked?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: In cross-examination? Mr. O'Sullivan asked this witness some questions relating to the material he received from the Viennese police officers when he asked for photocopies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I think the question probably was when did he receive --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The question asked was when did he receive those copies, not that he received any other thing apart from those copies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe he didn't -- defence counsel did not specifically get into the details of every single thing he received, but given that he raised the general issue of what this witness received from the Viennese police officers after he had requested photocopies, I believe it's fair re-examination. I will tell your Honours that, if necessary, we can recall this witness later on to specifically talk about this, but given that defence counsel has raised it, we believe it's fair re-examination and that it would just speed things along. Because this witness works in The Hague, if your Honours disagree, I am not objecting too strenuously, but we do believe it is fair re-examination, given that defence counsel has raised the issue. We believe the issue had not been raised in direct, but defence counsel chose to get into it in cross, and then as part of the re-examination the Prosecution is entitled to explore the issue raised by the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think you can -- if there is any need arising, we will give them an opportunity to examine on those.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: When did you receive these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe we received the documents around 20th March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: They are not part of the index which we admitted this morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe Mr. Moerbauer explained that they are not, in fact, part of the index because in making photocopies it appeared -- Mr. Moerbauer stated that the original was given to the Prosecution such that Mr. Moerbauer was able to say by going back to the copies he had made and kept for his own records that these documents, 147 -- that he did have the photocopies of them but that he did not have the originals and they were not part of his index. I believe he explained that. Is it 147A, B and C? Sir, I ask you to look at those documents and tell me if you recognise them and, if so, what they are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are the documents I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Show them to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. They have previously been provided to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The originals?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: The originals. They have been given copies of everything and allowed to inspect whatever they wished. Certainly I'm happy if any of them want to look at any of these documents again, to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe there is another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. So in other words there was -- I'm sorry, Mr. d'Hooge. Are you stating there was an additional document with those but that is also -- those documents were given to you at the time you received the photocopies as well as one additional document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so. The four documents were stapled together.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I only have three documents here.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. For the use of defence counsel, there was a fourth document which we do not believe is relevant. If defence counsel wishes to inspect that, we are happy to get it and provide it for you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination arising from this questioning?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to accept the offer to get that and let us inspect it, the document that they've decided is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose since the form has been spoken about the fourth one should be available for inspection.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I have the originial right now and I also have copies. I don't know which defence counsel would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Of the fourth one?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We had selected the documents that we thought were relevant and this was not one of them, but I'm happy to show it to defence counsel, and if they wish, they can show it to the witness. We have extra copies for defence counsel, if that would also assist. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Can I please look at the other documents as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would your Honours think it very rude of me if I went and peered over Mr. Ackerman's shoulder?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You can't read it. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): May I put a question to the witness in connection with this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can. You are free to. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. d'Hooge, can you tell me whether you speak Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Can you tell me when you were in Room 331 did you take these documents out of the cardboard box in which you said that the videotapes were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I believe I selected the document out of a folder. I didn't take them out.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Mr. d'Hooge, the folder was not in the cardboard box; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe the folder was on a table.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Mr. d'Hooge, the papers that you took out of the folder, did they have any recognisable indication for you, who does not speak Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, I didn't take the documents out of the folder. I selected them and repositioned them so it was easy for the Vienna police to make a copy to see what documents we wanted, and if I can see the documents I can indicate why I wanted a copy of that document to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm asking you, Mr. d'Hooge, whether in repositioning those documents you marked those documents with a sign that you can always recognise, since you do not speak Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't mark the documents. I only repositioned them.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: And such unmarked documents were given by you to one of the policemen of the Austrian police for photocopying; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I repeat that I did not take out the documents. I repositioned them in the folder.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did you ask that those documents be copied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Were they photocopied while you were still in Room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: In Room 331 there was no photocopying machine; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not the reason why they were not copied while we were there. The members of the Vienna police wanted to have authorisation of Dr. Seda, if they could, for the copy of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Therefore, while you were there between 5.00 and 7.30 pm on that day no documents were photocopied, because there was no authorisation from Dr. Seda; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Mr. d'Hooge, did you give these documents for experts to see and analyse the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you know at all when these documents were photocopied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that they were photocopied the moment that the Vienna police had authorisation from Dr. Seda, and I believe also that they couldn't get the authorisation the same day because it was after working hours and probably Dr. Seda was not in his office any more.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Are you sure, Mr. d'Hooge, that when you repositioned the documents, you didn't mark them with any recognisable number or mark?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: You have seen just now, sir, some marks on these papers beginning with "00". Did these numbers exist when you allegedly saw these papers in the Austrian police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you show me the documents? I don't know what the mark ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If you will oblige him, he might indicate to you how he chose him and how he recognised them. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Will you please be so kind as to tell us whether when you were repositioning those documents you saw the numbers that are now to be found on this paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The number was not on the document at that time. This is an internal from the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What were the marks, identification signs used in repositioning them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will explain, your Honour. Let's say this is a folder in which the document was. The document was like that. Since I found that this document was interesting, I put it like that in the same folder. I just repositioned it, which was clear for the Austrian police that this was a document that I wanted to be photocopied. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Would you please be so kind as to confirm something once again that I think you've said. These folders were on one of the tables in Room 331; Mr. d'Hooge, therefore you just said that those documents, as far as you can remember, or rather according to your knowledge were in a folder that was on one of the tables in Room 331 of the police building in Vienna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that the folders were on a table and I can be even more precise; when you enter the room, on the right side on a table.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: And you, Mr. d'Hooge, have no idea where they were -- they came from before they reached that table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If my memory is okay, I believe that we were told that they came from the premises of Inda-Bau.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: But at that point in time, Mr. d'Hooge, no folders or files had any marks that were recognisable by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: The moment you received these papers in The Hague several days later, they did not have the mark that you can now see on this paper; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Actually, they had no marking; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: This mark was placed later, after the paper reached the premises of the prosecution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is clearly an internal number from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one or two. I may be going outside of the scope of re-examination, but if I do, would the court stop me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, we will stop you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I am volunteering to be stopped. Mr. d'Hooge, do you recall on June 3rd I showed you this document, the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: And on re-examination Ms McHenry asked you if you had a copy of this with you in Vienna and you responded no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: I never asked you if you had a copy of it, did I?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember. It's possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: If I told you the transcript said I never asked you if you had a copy with you, would you take that as truthful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Would you take it on faith that the only question I asked you about it was whether or not the date on it was March 19th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Is the date on it still March 19th if it was on June 3rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: If the date that Richard Goldstone -- it shows Richard Goldstone signed it, when you looked at it on June 3rd, was March 19th, 1996, it would still be that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think this is all for this witness. So he can be discharged.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Any other witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would move into evidence the statement taken by the Office of the Prosecutor of Mr. Mucic as well as the statement taken by the Office of the Prosecutor of Mr. Delic and Mr. Landzo, and in just one minute I'll give you those numbers. The Prosecution would tender into evidence what has been marked for identification purposes as Prosecution Exhibit 101, which is Mr. Mucic's interview by the Office of the Prosecutor, and the video recording; Mr. Landzo's interview and the recording, which is 102; and Mr. Delic's interviews and the recordings, which are 103.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: That is not by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I know it has been a while, but on direct examination this witness discussed at length the fact that he was the person who took both -- all of them, all of these three interviews and he identified them and was cross-examined about the circumstances by all them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually that will not be the end of his evidence. This re-examination should not have been the end of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I am confused. On direct examination this witness testified and identified the interviews of Mr. Mucic taken by the Office of the Prosecutor, the interviews of Mr. Landzo and the interviews of Mr. Delic. He was cross-examined by the Defence attorneys, Mr. Mucic, Mr. Landzo and Mr. Delic about the circumstances of those statements, and we are now tendering them into evidence. It did not really come up today, because the -- it came up in direct examination. The cross-examinations of Mr. Landzo and Mr. Delic's counsel was last week, but this witness did testify about all of those issues, identified all those exhibits and was cross-examined about his testimony surrounding the giving and the taking of those interviews.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The proper challenges about the admissibility comes at the time you are tendering them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that we tendered them and defence counsel indicated and your Honours indicated that they preferred to wait until cross-examination for your Honours to actually rule on the issue: so now that cross-examination is completed, I am now re-tendering them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the matter is to be the subject of argument, I would rather do that tomorrow, please, when I have had an opportunity to review all the evidence that has been given concerning the admissibility of these interviews rather than do it this evening, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is an admitted position that these interviews were held and the individual they were video recorded and he is the gentleman who recorded these interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes, to all of those, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: They can be tendered now in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: They can now be tendered in evidence and whatever the probative value is can be seen later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I understand what your Honour is saying but there is a substantive motion before the Tribunal concerning admissibility. One would like to know when that matter is going to be argued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think this is the stage when actually you should argue it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Well, I anticipated that is what was being said. I hope that your Honour will be so kind as to give me overnight to review the evidence before addressing you on the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think that is the proper thing. We will have to come back tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am grateful to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is one matter I would like to raise before you rise this evening. Earlier today transcripts pages 6, lines 14-14 and page 8, lines 1-3 my learned friend Mr. Niemann, leading counsel for the Prosecution, made a sweeping allegation against all defence counsel in this case. Taking two matters into consideration, one that last week my learned friend Mr. Ackerman's graciously offered apologies were equally graciously accepted by my learned friend Ms McHenry and, two, that he has had a whole day to reflect on the words he spoke, all of my friends are wondering when Mr. Niemann has anything to say to your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, I'm not prepared to withdraw what I said. The comment I made was in relation to the failure of the Defence to give the opportunity to the Prosecution to review the videotape, which was in their possession and they could easily have done so. In my submission fair failure to do that was deliberate. In my submission that does not help the progress of these proceedings. So I'm not prepared to withdraw the allegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Is it your position that the allegation was intentionally made and that you did not regret it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I said was that in my submission the Defence were trying to take over the proceedings by this approach. It was highly inappropriate. They know better and they could have made this material available. It would have assisted the proceedings. It would have assisted the Prosecution, and they deliberately chose not to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: So you also deliberately made allegations. Now my position is that these are matters which might have happened in the heat of the moment and would have been regretted immediately after and there could be mutual apologies from either end. I don't think there is any point sticking to a position which could easily be solved.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases, I take your Honour's guidance on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose you will sleep over it and we will come tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am grateful to your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Trial Chamber will now rise. (5.10 pm)
